metadata.case_name: WONG YAN LAM v. INTERCONTINENTAL HIRE CARS LTD AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: Clerk at Gigamind International Education Development Co. Ltd. (a primary school)
plaintiff.occupation_after: Employed by her father-in-law in an engineering firm (since March 2009)
plaintiff.education_level: Diploma of Business (Royal Brisbane International College); incomplete Bachelor of Business Administration (University of Canberra, distance learning)

injuries.description: Multiple contusions to neck, right shoulder and low back
source: The doctors agree that in the first accident the plaintiff sustained multiple contusions to her neck, right shoulder and low back, but the medical reports indicate that she was probably making good progress by the time of the second accident, when she suffered a sprained neck and experienced right shoulder pain.

injuries.description: Sprained neck (second accident) with right shoulder pain
source: The doctors agree that in the first accident the plaintiff sustained multiple contusions to her neck, right shoulder and low back, but the medical reports indicate that she was probably making good progress by the time of the second accident, when she suffered a sprained neck and experienced right shoulder pain.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified strain or sprain of cervical spine

source: She was diagnosed as suffering from post traumatic stress disorder and referred to the clinical psychologist of Castle Peak Hospital, who prescribed anti-depressants.

manifestations.description: lost consciousness for a while and suffered dizziness when she came round and had severe pain over her head, neck, lower back and pelvis
severe pain in her head and all over her body
limited movement in the neck and shoulders
tenderness over the posterior aspect and slight stiffness (neck)
constant headache and inability to sleep
fear of travelling (anxiety when travelling on buses)
emotional disturbance and flash back of the accidents
weakness of the right upper limb and pain on lifting things
paraesthesia and weakness of the ulnar thenar finger
vomits froth every two or three days; blurred vision; afraid of bright light (requires constant wearing of sun glasses)
inability to write properly and to write for more than about 10 minutes at a time (claimed by plaintiff)

treatments_received: ambulance transport to Caritas Medical Centre
A&E treatment (Caritas Medical Centre; Queen Elizabeth Hospital)
MRI and X-ray examinations (cervical and lumbar spine, brain)
psychiatric and psychological treatment (Castle Peak Hospital clinical psychologist)
treatments_future: psychiatric treatment (one year) suggested by psychiatrists

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Can no longer enjoy her hobbies and sporting activities such as badminton nor continue the voluntary work she enjoyed.

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: Anxious when travelling on buses; fear of travelling.
Poor memory and impaired concentration; insomnia; nightmares; emotional disturbance and flashbacks.

losses.category: Loss of ability to pursue education
losses.description: Had to discontinue studying for a BBA degree with the University of Canberra as the inability to write for more than a few minutes prevented her from taking the last examination she needed to complete it (as claimed).
